title: Why Is the Sky Blue?
narration: Sunlight looks white, but it carries every colour of the visible spectrum. So why does the sky look blue? As sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere, tiny gas molecules scatter shorter blue wavelengths more strongly than longer red wavelengths. The blue light spreads in every direction, and some of it reaches your eyes from across the sky. Scientists call this Rayleigh scattering. It is why a clear daytime sky usually appears blue, while the colours near sunset can look very different.

sources.title: Why Is the Sky Blue?
sources.supports: Sunlight is scattered by gases and particles in the atmosphere; blue light is scattered more than other colours because it has shorter wavelengths.
